clue.text: One providing shock treatment?

parts.note: a shock here is a thick mass of hair, not an electric jolt, so the treatment is a cut or a set at a salon

explanation.surface: A doctor administering electroconvulsive therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock treatment' suggests electric therapy; a shock of hair is a bushy head of it, and the person who treats that works in a salon.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylist is the professional who cuts and styles a client's shock of hair.

clue.text: He built a wall with unfinished and broken handrail

indicators.note: broken means the remaining letters are smashed up and rearranged
unfinished means the word handrail loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A builder working on a wall with a damaged, half-made handrail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the L from HANDRAIL, leaving HANDRAI, and 'broken' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor ordered the great barrier across northern England in AD 122.

clue.text: Get used to being in old city quarter

parts.note: being in somewhere is being in it, taken as written
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone settling into life in a historic district of an ancient town.
explanation.definitionFit: To harden or accustom someone to something unpleasant is to make them used to it.

clue.text: A number lead the union in time-wasting action

indicators.note: lead means the number goes in front of the next piece

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
an alliance is a union of parties

explanation.surface: A trade-union song is used to stall negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number lead' reads like a musical number; here the Roman numeral D leads, going first.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallying is idling or trifling, so it is a way of frittering away time.

clue.text: Goes out after a rise

parts.note: the tide comes in and rises, then recedes again

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the house after getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a person rising from bed and going out; the subject is the sea, which retreats after the flood tide.
explanation.definitionFit: The receding of the tide after high water is its falling away.

clue.text: Associate party with enjoyment

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or contest
a kick is a thrill or pleasure, as in getting a kick out of something

explanation.surface: Linking a political party with having fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a sidekick is a close companion or assistant.

clue.text: Used by cars in Greek island, say

indicators.note: say means the island's name is spoken and the word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: Motorists driving around a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Highways and streets are what motor traffic travels on.

clue.text: French official with authority over the lower classes?

definitions.text: with authority over the lower classes?

explanation.surface: A Parisian bureaucrat with power over the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower classes' sounds social; it is the junior forms of a school, which senior pupils help supervise.
explanation.definitionFit: In France a préfet heads a department's administration; in a British school a senior pupil keeps order among the younger ones.

clue.text: Time turns around it

indicators.note: turns means the letters of around it are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A clock whose hands go round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of time, how long something lasts, is its span.

clue.text: Basic support for sleeping partners?

parts.note: sleeping partners sounds like silent investors in a firm needing financial support; read literally it is a couple asleep, who need furniture to lie on

explanation.surface: Funding arrangements for silent investors in a business.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeping partner in Britain is an investor who takes no active part in a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples sleep together on a bed made for two people.

clue.text: Lincoln protected America from corrupt practice

indicators.note: protected means the first piece surrounds and shelters the second

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of President Abraham Lincoln
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: President Lincoln shielded his country from corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuse or improper treatment, such as abuse of power, is a corrupt practice.

clue.text: A brie I ordered from Spain and Portugal

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of a brie I are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A diner ordering French cheese from Iberian suppliers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like placing an order with a shop; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula in south-west Europe shared by the two countries has this name.

clue.text: Blue picture?

parts.note: a blue picture suggests a pornographic film, but here it is a painting of the blue heavens

explanation.surface: A risqué film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' as smutty is the trap; the picture shows the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting or view whose subject is the sky and clouds is this kind of picture.

clue.text: Snooping, a small number make notes

parts.note: No. is the short form of number
to sing is to produce musical notes with the voice

explanation.surface: A few people spying and jotting things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' suggests writing; it means producing musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Prying into others' business is poking one's nose in.

clue.text: Arrange to see her in Oxford, perhaps?

indicators.note: arrange means the letters of to see her are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Organising a visit to a woman in the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is not the city but a lace-up shoe, which keeps its shape with this device inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaped block put inside footwear to keep its form is placed in an Oxford brogue, for example.

clue.text: Bill is cut short, strange to tell

indicators.note: cut short means the word is trimmed back to its first two letters

parts.note: an account is a bill to be paid
quaint means odd or old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Bill's speech was oddly abbreviated, strange to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is an invoice, ACCOUNT, abbreviated to AC as in a/c.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform someone or make them familiar with facts is to tell them.

clue.text: Such is life on the rolling deep

definitions.text: Such is life on the rolling deep

parts.words: Such is life on the rolling deep
parts.note: on a rolling sea a ship rises and falls, just as life has its ups and downs

explanation.surface: A sailor's philosophical shrug about life at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Life on a heaving ocean, like life generally, has good and bad times alternating.

clue.text: A direction to shed hot weather wear

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
to undress is to shed one's clothes

explanation.surface: Instructions to take clothes off in the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sleeveless frock is worn in summer sunshine.

clue.text: An unpleasant task for little Augustus — the choir master

parts.note: a chore is a tedious job
Gus is a pet form of the name Augustus

explanation.surface: A tedious job given to a boy called Augustus by the choirmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: In ancient Athens the choregus was the citizen who paid for and led a dramatic chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek term names the leader or sponsor of a chorus, a choir master in effect.

clue.text: A strong case for hard currency

definitions.text: A strong case for hard currency

parts.words: A strong case for hard currency
parts.note: a strong case sounds like a persuasive argument, but it is a sturdy container holding coins and notes

explanation.surface: A good argument in favour of a stable currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong case' reads as a convincing argument; it is a robust box, and hard currency is coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A lockable metal container is where money is kept safe.

clue.text: An attractive bar in which we saw Bunter

explanation.surface: A pleasant pub where we spotted a schoolboy character.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter, the greedy schoolboy of Greyfriars, appeared in the British boys' weekly paper of this name from 1908 to 1940.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of iron attracts metal; the paper of that title ran the Billy Bunter stories.

clue.text: Sort of bus you take round supermarkets

explanation.surface: A bus that ferries shoppers around stores.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolleybus draws power from overhead wires; shoppers push a wheeled basket round the aisles.

clue.text: Annul, even in court?

parts.note: a higher court can cancel the verdict of a lower one; the question mark flags a phrase splitting into words that suggest evening up a contest

explanation.surface: Cancelling a decision, even in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom setting is apt: an appeal court quashes, or annuls, an earlier judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge cancelling a ruling is said to quash or annul it.

clue.text: Take notice, but don't retire

explanation.surface: Advice to pay attention and keep working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retire' sounds like giving up work; here it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To become suddenly attentive is one sense; staying awake instead of going to bed is the other.

clue.text: Slowly executed movement gets a soldier in trouble

indicators.note: in means the soldier piece is placed inside the trouble piece

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier marching slowly gets into a spot of bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests marching; it is a section of a symphony played slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement of music played at a slow tempo carries this Italian marking.

clue.text: Subject someone to heated questioning?

parts.note: heated suggests angry interrogation, but it also suggests cooking under intense heat

explanation.surface: Police interrogating a suspect fiercely.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate intensively is one sense; to cook under direct heat is the other.

clue.text: Two similar notes required for one in operatic role

indicators.note: two similar means the note piece appears twice in a row

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer needs a pair of identical notes for a part in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The consumptive seamstress in Puccini's La Bohème is the heroine role.

clue.text: A sheepish expression?

parts.note: sheepish suggests embarrassed, but here it means coming from a sheep

explanation.surface: An embarrassed look on someone's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish expression' sounds like a guilty face; it is the sound a sheep makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of a ewe or lamb is what a sheep utters.

clue.text: Leader may turn out to be real idiot

indicators.note: turn out means the letters of real idiot turn into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor may prove to be a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a person; in Britain it is also the main opinion article in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article giving its opinion is also called a leader.

clue.text: "Look back in anger" performed at oberammergau?

definitions.text: "Look back in anger" performed at oberammergau?

parts.words: Look back in anger" performed at oberammergau
parts.note: anger is a strong emotion, and Look Back in Anger is a stage drama, so a drama of strong emotion staged at Oberammergau suggests the Bavarian village's famous religious drama

explanation.surface: John Osborne's play staged in a Bavarian village.
explanation.walkthrough: Look Back in Anger is John Osborne's 1956 British play; Oberammergau in Bavaria has staged a drama of Christ's suffering every ten years since 1634.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatisation of Christ's suffering and death is staged at Oberammergau each decade.
